text:
anne: Heads-up — new canary for sablev2-int4 looks fine on latency/cost but funcall JSON parse failures jumped from ~2% -> ~7% after the quantized path was enabled. Happening on streaming + kv-prefix workloads. Anyone seen a kv-prefix + int4 interaction before?

mike: Ugh. Do we have an example payload? stack traces or raw model output?

anne: Pasting one raw model output we captured (streamed fragment):
```
{"tool":"lookup","args":{"id":123}}
...
]}
}
extra_tokens: @@
```
Seems like truncated/mangled suffixes appended after a close-brace, not valid JSON. Not typical stray whitespace.

sasha: :eyes: That looks like a streaming boundary hit where kvcache prefix plus continuous batching changed tokenization alignment. int4 kernels sometimes produce different EOS behavior. Did we enable the new kernel-selection heuristics in canary?

anne: We flipped the int4 kernel selector for perf (it picked fast-path). Canary config is default streaming + kv-prefix caching.

canary-bot: Alert: structured_output_parse_errors increased 5.1% in sablev2-int4-canary (last 30m). sample_count=1240.

mike: Quick triage suggestions — 1) capture raw token ids for failing traces, 2) run same prompt on float16 mirror and compare token sequences, 3) try disabling kv-prefix caching in canary to see if rate drops.

anne: I'll dump token ids + model logits for a few failing traces. I can also do a quick 2h AB where we disable kv-prefix for 10% traffic.

sasha: Also watch retry budget interaction — our parser-rescue was kicking in and issuing a retry which can inflate downstream failures/billing. If we change canary behavior, ensure no extra retries. Maybe add a light postprocess repair: wrap NDJSON per-line parse attempt and then strict validate, so we don't immediately retry.

mike: Good call. As temporary mitigation we could 1) traffic split 90/10 (float16 fallback), 2) disable kv-prefix caching on int4 route, 3) turn off automatic retry-on-parse-failure for that route.

anne: Plan (quick):
- run token-id diffs vs f16 mirror (ETA 30m)
- roll 10% traffic to f16 fallback (if diffs show suffix mismatch)
- disable kv-prefix caching in canary (A/B)
- add NDJSON soft-repair in postprocess for streaming path
- collect 1k failing+ok samples and open a bench with runtime team

sasha: sounds reasonable. One more: add a small sentinel at end-of-output ("<<END_OUTPUT>>") in canary prompts to make streaming boundary explicit for parser — only for canary.

anne: I'll push the sentinel + token capture now, then start the 10% fallback. Will post results.

mike: Thx — ping us when you have the token diffs. :thumbsup:

anne: ping — token diffs show that int4 path occasionally emits an extra control token (id 50234) right after closing brace before EOS, which the parser treats as content. f16 mirror doesn't.

sasha: OK that matches the kv-prefix alignment hypothesis. We'll file a runtime bug for kernel selection fallback + add a canary-only heal (sentinel + NDJSON).

anne: Created runtime bug: RUNTIME-3521. Created canary patch and will shepherd rollout.

mike: Nice. Keep the canary-bot alerts on. If failure rate doesn't drop after the fixes, escalate to ops.

anne: Will do. Thanks all. :pray:

canary-bot: Note: automated canary snapshot saved -> s3://redwood-canary/sablev2-int4/6765432100/snapshot-1.json
